instructions: Put the rice in a sieve and rinse it under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Drain the lentils and rinse them. Finely chop the onion and grate the garlic.
Heat 4 tbsp of the olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and golden at the edges.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the bay leaf and 1/4 tsp pepper. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the rice and the remaining 1 tsp salt and stir for 1 minute. Add the lentils and 1 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Don't lift the lid before then.
Take the pan off the heat and remove the bay leaf. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and fluff the pilaf with a fork, stirring in the parsley and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.
Cut the lemon into wedges. Serve with the lemon wedges and the olives.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lemon.
method_notes: Dimitras Dishes (no rating shown) is the lead: onion, garlic and canned tomatoes in olive oil, then rice and lentils together with a bay leaf and a covered 15 minute simmer, finished with parsley, lemon and olives. Olive Tomato and Carol the Greek cook dried lentils separately and add carrot (and celery) before the rice; they run 50 to 65 minutes. To reach about 35 minutes this uses canned lentils (Carol the Greek allows cooked lentils) and skips the 15 minute rice soak, so it runs a few minutes over 30. It is vegan as written, and the lead's optional feta was left off.
